scope: Twenty-eight freshly reviewed, source-backed additions: one console-to-mobile static recompilation, seven software/protocol reimplementations, and twenty MiSTer FPGA system cores.

projects.title: Resident Evil Gaiden: Recompiled (Android)
projects.game: Resident Evil Gaiden (Game Boy Color, 2001; USA ROM)
projects.platform: Game Boy Color → Windows x86-64, Android ARM64-v8a (Android 7.0+/API 24+, OpenGL ES 3)
projects.status: Android v0.4.1 APK published 2026-09-16. The maintainer marks Android ARM64-v8a as fully supported and documents touch controls; the README does not state a named physical-device test matrix or claim a complete playthrough. Latest repository push reported by GitHub was 2026-09-16.
projects.summary: Game-specific native static recompilation of Resident Evil Gaiden from the Game Boy Color USA ROM to C/C++ with SDL2 and OpenGL ES 3. Android builds target ARM64-v8a with minSdk 24 (Android 7.0+) and include a touch gamepad. Players must supply the exact legally acquired Resident Evil Gaiden (USA).gbc ROM (2,097,152 bytes; expected SHA-256 9a97678cbd8da02c8763e977674e17f460c06ea8b73bad35c52fe6817f506d44); the repository and APK do not include the ROM or commercial game assets.
projects.strategy: Game-specific native static recompilation of the GBC title into C/C++ with an SDL2 platform layer and OpenGL ES 3 Android rendering.
projects.source_available: Public source repository and v0.4.1 Android ARM64 APK release; user supplies the exact USA ROM. The repository and release omit copyrighted ROM data and commercial game assets.
projects.subtype: Game-specific Android ARM64-v8a recompilation

projects.title: OpenADS (Advantage Database Server compatibility implementation)
projects.game: SAP Advantage Database Server and Advantage Client Engine API
projects.platform: Windows, Linux, and macOS are covered by upstream CI; the compatibility libraries expose ace32.dll, ace64.dll, and libace.so names. Backend and packaging support vary by platform.
projects.status: Active; GitHub lists OpenADS v1.09.74 published 2026-10-12, with source pushed through that release date. The README reports 442/442 Harbour rddtst.prg compatibility tests passing on Windows MSVC64 (2026-05-08), but documents data-dictionary and access-control parity gaps and says untrusted or multi-user use remains experimental. The README status paragraph still names v1.09.68, so its embedded release reference lags the GitHub release page.
projects.summary: An independent implementation compatible with the discontinued SAP Advantage Database Server, exposing Advantage Client Engine entry points as a drop-in library/server for existing applications. Upstream explicitly calls its provenance clean-room and says it is based on publicly observable ACE behavior and the public Harbour rddads call site; it does not claim full feature parity, and documents significant deployment limits.
projects.strategy: Upstream-declared clean-room ACE API implementation based on observable behavior and public Harbour rddads call-site source; exposes compatible client-library entry points and a server protocol.
projects.source_available: Public source under Apache License 2.0.
projects.subtype: Advantage Client Engine API-compatible database library and server

projects.title: Open Bamboo Networking (Bambu Studio network-plugin replacement)
projects.game: Bambu Studio's proprietary bambu_networking plugin and Bambu Lab printer communications
projects.platform: Linux x86_64 and aarch64 and Windows x64 are primary targets; Windows ARM64 and macOS ARM64/x86_64 are experimental. Upstream also supports Orca Slicer with caveats.
projects.status: Active; latest release v2.2.0 was published 2026-09-24 and the canonical repository received source updates through 2026-10-14. The README lists Bambu Studio plugin ABI series 02.03.00.xx through 02.08.04.xx and Orca Slicer v2.3.2 or newer. LAN printing and device features are mainly tested on a Bambu Lab P2S; other model/firmware combinations vary. The default LAN path requires printer Developer Mode; some cloud features need credentials supplied by the user. Go Live and HMS photo snapshot are listed as unimplemented.
projects.summary: A native drop-in replacement for Bambu Studio's separately distributed proprietary networking plugin. It reproduces the plugin's dlsym ABI and printer-facing behavior using public protocol references plus observations from MITM captures; it is a substantial library implementation, not a wrapper around the closed plugin. The README does not claim a clean-room process.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineered, binary-compatible replacement for the closed plugin ABI and printer protocols; upstream credits public protocol projects and MITM captures, with no clean-room claim in the reviewed README.
projects.source_available: Public source under GNU Affero General Public License version 3.0 (AGPL-3.0).
projects.subtype: Binary-compatible slicer network-plugin replacement

sources.label: Canonical maintainer README: plugin replacement goal, protocol basis, supported systems and slicer ABI versions, status and feature limits

It does not use vendor client code or resources, and the README does not explicitly label the project clean-room.
projects.strategy: Independent client and protocol implementation based on observable network behavior and published standards; no explicit clean-room label found in the reviewed README.
projects.source_available: Public source and documentation under Apache License 2.0.

projects.title: OpenBRCM (Broadcom 43xx Linux Wi-Fi driver)
projects.game: Broadcom BCM4352 PCIe SoftMAC Wi-Fi controller (PCI ID 14e4:43b1) and related 43xx hardware
projects.platform: Out-of-tree Linux kernel driver using mac80211/cfg80211, BCMA, and firmware-loader APIs. The MVP target is BCM4352 on kernel 7.x; upstream says Linux 6.12 build compatibility is pending.
projects.status: Early implementation; no tagged release. The README identifies BCM4352 (14e4:43b1) as the MVP device and reports hardware-proven isolated firmware, initialization, and DMA tests. At the checked revision, RX frame completion and interface bring-up remain unproven, 5 GHz and interface bring-up are disabled, and it is not a complete usable Wi-Fi driver. The latest source push in GitHub metadata was 2026-09-28.
projects.summary: A Linux kernel driver written from scratch for Broadcom 43xx PCIe SoftMAC controllers, intended to replace functionality in a proprietary hybrid driver. The upstream explicitly calls it clean-room and says implementation is derived from a separate reverse-engineering specification and public silicon behavior, with no code copied from the proprietary blob or other drivers. Its current hardware validation is limited to isolated subsystems.
projects.strategy: Upstream-declared clean-room Linux driver implementation based on a separate reverse-engineering specification and public silicon documentation; no proprietary driver code is included according to its provenance policy.
projects.source_available: Public source under GNU General Public License version 2 only (GPL-2.0-only).
projects.subtype: Broadcom PCIe SoftMAC Wi-Fi kernel driver

sources.label: Maintainer README: target controller, kernel target, current status and known gaps

projects.title: open_ring (Oura Ring 4 BLE protocol driver)
projects.game: Oura Ring 4 Bluetooth Low Energy protocol
projects.platform: Python host-side BLE implementation using bleak; the README does not provide a tested host-operating-system matrix.
projects.status: No tagged release; the repository's last source push in GitHub metadata was 2026-05-11. The README says the protocol is fully mapped and reports structural decoding of 953,206 records across 40 captures with zero decode errors. These are maintainer-reported verification results, not an independent audit.
projects.summary: A Python BLE driver, decoder and analytics toolkit for Oura Ring 4 data. The README calls it a clean-room toolkit but also says its development used static reverse engineering of native shared objects from the official Android application, as well as empirical BLE captures. It is therefore recorded as a reverse-engineered protocol implementation, with the upstream clean-room label and its disclosed binary-analysis basis both preserved.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineered BLE protocol driver; upstream self-describes it as clean-room but discloses static reverse engineering of the official Android app's native shared objects, so the self-label is recorded with that methodological caveat.
projects.source_available: Public source under GNU General Public License version 3.0 (GPL-3.0).
projects.subtype: Bluetooth Low Energy device-protocol driver and data decoder

sources.label: Maintainer README: Ring 4 target, self-described clean-room status, disclosed static analysis basis, coverage and project status

projects.title: ork-driver (Rockchip RK35xx NPU matmul library)
projects.game: Rockchip RK35xx NPU register-command ISA and matmul execution path
projects.platform: ARM64 Rockchip Linux userspace on systems with the in-tree rknpu DRM kernel driver; not a kernel module. RK3588 is hardware-validated, RK3576 is listed as needing on-device validation, and RK3562/RK3568 support is not yet added.
projects.status: Active development; source was pushed through 2026-10-14 and no tagged release is listed. Upstream reports RK3588 validation on a Radxa ROCK 5B for fp16, int8/w8a8 and int4 matrix multiplication, with example workloads compared against CPU references. The RK3576 path uses inherited tuning parameters and still needs device validation. This is a focused matmul implementation, not a full API-compatible replacement for Rockchip's proprietary runtime.
projects.summary: A clean-room userspace library that synthesizes Rockchip NPU register-command programs and submits them through the open rknpu DRM kernel driver. Upstream says it reverse-engineered the regcmd instruction set from scratch and does not use proprietary librknnrt; the library implements matmul functionality rather than the full proprietary inference-runtime API.
projects.strategy: Upstream-declared clean-room reimplementation of the RK35xx register-command execution path for matmul, using the existing open rknpu kernel driver; not an API-compatible full SDK replacement.
projects.source_available: Public source under the ISC License.
projects.subtype: Userspace NPU matmul library and direct hardware driver

sources.label: Maintainer README: clean-room claim, NPU interface, proprietary-runtime boundary, supported SoCs and hardware validation

projects.title: TVT IPTool for Linux (TVT camera and NVR network provisioning)
projects.game: TVT-family IP-camera, NVR, and DVR discovery and network-provisioning protocols
projects.platform: Linux x86_64. GTK 3 build is documented for Ubuntu 18.04-era/glibc 2.27 systems; GTK 4 build targets Ubuntu 24.04/current Debian, with Fedora build instructions.
projects.status: Latest tagged release v0.1.5 was published 2026-07-15; the repository's last source push was also 2026-07-15 and it is not archived. The README calls this the first release and lists device discovery, IPv4 provisioning, and verification. It does not identify a specific TVT model or firmware compatibility matrix; routed-subnet scanning, IPv6 provisioning, activation, and firmware upgrades are outside the stated scope.
projects.summary: A native Linux C/GTK utility that directly implements TVT-family Layer-2 discovery and network provisioning, with SSDP/UPnP response parsing and an authenticated NVR web API path. Upstream labels it clean-room and says the application ships no vendor SDK binaries, headers, credentials, firmware, or assets; discovery and IP changes do not require the optional SDK loader. It is a focused provisioning client, not a full replacement for the vendor application.
projects.strategy: Upstream-labeled clean-room C/GTK client that implements TVT network discovery and provisioning directly; the README does not document a source-denied specification workflow, so no stronger process claim is inferred.
projects.source_available: Public source under the MIT License.
projects.subtype: Linux camera/NVR discovery and network-provisioning utility

sources.label: Maintainer README: clean-room label, implemented protocols, scope, platforms, and SDK boundary

projects.platform: Oric-1 / Oric Atmos and Pravetz 8D 8-bit computers on MiSTer FPGA
projects.status: Maintained FPGA core; upstream source last pushed 2026-06-11. The README documents tape loading, snapshots, ULA/video/6502/VIA/AY hardware and Pravetz 8D disk support. The latest checked-in RBF is dated 2026-06-03, close to the repository’s 2026-06-11 source update.
projects.summary: MiSTer FPGA hardware core for Oric-1 and Oric Atmos systems, including a Pravetz 8D compatibility option. The public source has no declared GitHub license; the tracked source tree includes a Microdisc ROM binary with no separate firmware rights statement.
projects.strategy: FPGA core ported from earlier MiST/SiDi Oric work, recreating the Oric CPU, ULA video, VIA, AY sound, tape and disk paths.
projects.source_available: Public source repository, but GitHub reports no declared license. A Microdisc ROM binary is tracked in the repository and its redistribution rights were not established; tape images and other system ROMs require separate rights.
projects.subtype: MiSTer FPGA vintage-computer hardware emulator core

projects.title: Colour Genie (EACA EG2000) MiSTer Core
projects.game: EACA Colour Genie / EG2000 software and cassette programs
projects.platform: EACA EG2000 Colour Genie home computer on MiSTer FPGA
projects.status: Runnable FPGA port with maintenance unclear; upstream last pushed 2025-09-08 and a release RBF is dated 2025-09-06. The README describes a from-scratch core and the Colour Genie’s original/upgraded text and graphics modes, BASIC and cassette loading.
projects.summary: MiSTer FPGA core for the EACA EG2000 Colour Genie home computer, an early TRS-80-compatible European system. The README describes cassette-based BASIC/machine-code loading; no firmware or software images were found in the tracked tree.
projects.strategy: FPGA hardware recreation/port of the Colour Genie implementation to MiSTer and other Altera FPGA boards.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-3.0 source repository. No system ROM or software images were found in the tracked tree; cassette images and any required ROMs must be supplied from separately obtained media.
projects.subtype: MiSTer FPGA vintage-computer hardware emulator core

projects.title: Atari System 2 MiSTer Core
projects.game: Paperboy, 720 Degrees, Super Sprint, Championship Sprint and APB arcade software
projects.platform: Atari System 2 arcade hardware on MiSTer FPGA
projects.status: Active hardware core; source last pushed 2026-09-25 and the repository contains a 2026-09-25 RBF. One bitstream supports the five System 2 games listed in the README; the launched MRA selects the title.
projects.summary: FPGA hardware recreation of Atari System 2, built around the DEC T-11 game CPU and a 6502/YM2151/dual-POKEY/TMS5220 sound board with Slapstic protection. Game ROMs are not included; the core uses user-provided MAME-compatible dumps.
projects.strategy: FPGA hardware recreation of Atari System 2, with the README documenting the reconstructed board components and five supported arcade titles.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-3.0 source repository. No game ROMs are included; users supply legally obtained MAME-compatible dumps. The README says a Paperboy prototype set is incomplete in MAME.
projects.subtype: MiSTer FPGA arcade hardware emulator core

projects.title: IGS PolyGame Master MiSTer Core
projects.game: Software for supported IGS PolyGame Master arcade cartridges
projects.platform: IGS PolyGame Master (PGM) arcade system on MiSTer FPGA
projects.status: Beta and actively tested; upstream source last pushed 2026-09-10 and the repository includes release bitstreams. The README says most games work but the platform’s many variants and bootlegs still need testing, and lists supported and not-yet-working sets individually.
projects.summary: MiSTer FPGA core for IGS’s cartridge-based PolyGame Master arcade platform. It models PGM-specific CPUs, sprite/video, sound, protection and battery-backed state; the user must provide MAME-compatible game and parent BIOS dumps.
projects.strategy: FPGA hardware emulation of the IGS PGM board, with per-game support and protection work documented in the upstream README.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-2.0 source repository. BIOS and cartridge dumps are not included; user-provided MAME-compatible files are required. README labels the core beta and says multiple variants/bootlegs remain untested.
projects.subtype: MiSTer FPGA arcade hardware emulator core

projects.title: Marble Madness II MiSTer Core
projects.game: Marble Madness II: Marble Man arcade prototype
projects.platform: Atari Games Marble Madness II prototype arcade board on MiSTer FPGA
projects.status: Active, hardware-validated core; upstream source last pushed 2026-10-08 and the latest checked-in RBF is dated 2026-09-04. The README reports that its MRA loads the full prototype ROM set and documents focused simulation plus real-ROM CPU/audio reset regressions.
projects.summary: FPGA hardware implementation for Atari Games’ unreleased 1991 Marble Madness II prototype. The source includes a hardware-validation note, but no game ROM is distributed; a legally obtained prototype MAME ROM set is required.
projects.strategy: FPGA recreation of the Marble Madness II prototype board, with a cycle-compatible Motorola 68000, JSA audio, trackball support and EEPROM persistence.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-3.0 source repository. The prototype game ROM set is explicitly not included and must be obtained separately; no redistribution right for game ROMs is implied by the core source license.
projects.subtype: MiSTer FPGA arcade hardware emulator core
